title: bug(cli): cancelled/panicked/deadline outcomes are flattened to FSNOW-9001 at the CLI edge
description:
## Background

docs/agent_cli_contract.md: "A cancelled query is outcome_kind = cancelled, not an error", and
the plan routes CancelKind (User, Deadline, CostBudget, Shutdown, ...) distinctly. Agents need to
tell "I cancelled it" from "it broke".

## Evidence

crates/franken-snowflake-cli/src/live.rs:1826-1842 (execute_request) and :974-983 (query cancel)
map Outcome::Cancelled and Outcome::Panicked to FSNOW-9001 Internal, exit 74. The envelope can
never say `cancelled`; `timeout` appears only for a server 408; the distinct CostBudget exit is
unreachable. SnowflakeOutcomeExt is unused outside core and driver tests.

## Scope

1. Cancelled(reason) -> outcome_kind `cancelled` (User, Shutdown, ParentCancelled) or `timeout`
   (Deadline, PollQuota), CancelKind in error.evidence, statement handle and remote-cancel
   result in data.
2. Exit codes: the contract table has no "cancelled" code. Decide and document (recommendation:
   add exit 8 = cancelled; keep 5 for deadline/budget exhaustion) in agent_cli_contract.md,
   agent-handbook and capabilities.exit_codes.
3. Panicked -> FSNOW-9002 with a redacted payload summary.
4. Receipts record terminal states even without rows (cancelled / timeout / failed).

## Tests

Scripted transport (cfg(test) execute seam) producing each outcome -> envelope + exit asserted.
Negative case a naive mapping fails: outcome_kind=error for Cancelled(User).
acceptance_criteria: Closes only when the named tests/probes in the description pass, including the stated negative case; cite evidence in the close comment.
notes: Reality-check key: C6. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.
close_reason:
CLOSED (self-verified; not independently verified). Evidence, 2026-09-24:
1. Cancelled(reason) -> FSNOW-5004 with outcome_kind `timeout` (Deadline/Timeout) or `cancelled` (every other kind), cancel_kind in error.evidence (`outcome_into_result`, `failure_outcome`).
2. Exit codes follow the existing core cancel policy (5 deadline/timeout/poll-quota/shutdown/drain, 2 cost budget, 0 user) and are documented in docs/agent_cli_contract.md. Deviation from the bead's recommendation: no new exit 8; the core policy already existed and is tested.
3. Panicked -> FSNOW-9001 with the redacted payload summary. Deviation: FSNOW-9002 is already SurfaceReserved.
4. A statement that ends without rows writes a receipt with receipt_state failed/cancelled/timed_out, the error code and cancel kind (local_store TerminalFailure); success receipts' canonical form is unchanged apart from the new build/query_tag fields.
Tests: core cancelled_error_exits_by_cancel_kind / cancelled_error_projects_like_the_cancel_it_carries; live outcome_into_result_keeps_cancel_kind_and_panic_summary (all four variants), scripted_cancellations_reach_the_envelope_by_kind (Deadline -> timeout exit 5, PollQuota -> cancelled exit 5, CostBudget -> cancelled exit 2, receipt_state read back through `receipt show`), scripted_query_failure_is_a_typed_error_envelope_with_a_failed_receipt (the old test asserted no receipt; the contract changed on purpose). Negative case: outcome_kind=error for a cancellation fails these assertions.

title: security(auth): quarantine the workload-identity lane — non-conformant protocol and unvalidated token URL
description:
## Background

The `workload_identity` auth lane (commits 49f5d6b, 7aa7aeb, 2026-09-19/20) is live-reachable but
implements a protocol Snowflake does not document for the SQL API, and it can send the OIDC
assertion to an arbitrary host in cleartext.

## Evidence

- It posts an RFC 7523 jwt-bearer grant to `/oauth/token-request`
  (crates/franken-snowflake-auth/src/workload_identity.rs:33, 42, 322, 537-544).
- Snowflake's documented SQL API WIF: `Authorization: Bearer WIF.{provider}.{token}` with
  `X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_FEDERATION`, provider in
  {AWS, AZURE, GCP, OIDC}, the provider token sent directly — no exchange step
  (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/authenticating, section "Using workload
  identity federation", consulted 2026-09-23).
- The token URL comes from `<PREFIX>_OIDC_TOKEN_URL` / `_TOKEN_URL` verbatim
  (crates/franken-snowflake-cli/src/live.rs ~2008) with no https or host validation, unlike the
  SQL API endpoint.
- Exchanged once at connection setup (live.rs 1775-1791); headers_at errors on expiry
  (workload_identity.rs:673); CHANGELOG claims mid-flight refresh.
- AGENTS.md:128: WIF only after PAT/JWT/OAuth are stable; none is live-proven since June.

## Scope

1. `AUTH=workload_identity` -> typed refusal before any socket (new FSNOW-2005 "workload identity
   lane not yet conformant with Snowflake's documented SQL API protocol; see bead C7").
2. `profile validate` reports the lane as `experimental_refused`.
3. Keep the existing code behind a default-off cargo feature (`wif-rfc7523-experimental`) rather
   than deleting it (no feature loss; may serve a future OAuth flow), excluded from release builds.
4. README/CHANGELOG corrected via A1.

## Tests

Live-build query run with AUTH=workload_identity -> FSNOW-2005, no socket (assert via scripted
seam that no request is attempted); validate reports the status. Negative: a quarantine that only
edits docs fails the no-request assertion.
acceptance_criteria: Closes only when the named tests/probes in the description pass, including the stated negative case; cite evidence in the close comment.
notes: Reality-check key: C7a. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.
close_reason:
CLOSED (self-verified; not independently verified). Evidence, 2026-09-24:
- LiveConn::resolve refuses a quarantined lane (workload_identity / workload_identity_federation / oidc) before any credential is read or request built; `profile validate` reports it as unusable (exit 3); health/capabilities list only pat, key_pair_jwt, oauth_bearer; the auth crate refuses a non-https token endpoint.
- Tests: cli_e2e workload_identity_lane_is_refused_before_any_request (live build: exit 3, FSNOW-2002, message names the quarantine, not the endpoint rule, which runs later); profile_validate_refuses_unusable_profiles covers the quarantined lane; auth test_cleartext_token_endpoint_is_refused.
Deviation: the refusal code is FSNOW-2002 ProfileInvalid rather than the FSNOW-2005 the bead text named (no such code exists in the registry). The library implementation stays for C7 (implement Snowflake's documented WIF.<provider>.<token> scheme).

title: feat(auth): Snowflake workload identity federation per the documented SQL API protocol (AWS/Azure/GCP/OIDC)
description:
## Background

AGENTS.md auth lane #4: workload identity federation (keyless auth for agents running on cloud
workloads), implemented only after PAT, key-pair JWT and OAuth are stable. C7a quarantines the
current non-conformant implementation; this bead implements the documented protocol.

## Protocol (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/authenticating, "Using workload
identity federation", consulted 2026-09-23 — re-verify before implementing and record the date)

- Header: `Authorization: Bearer WIF.{AWS|AZURE|GCP|OIDC}.{token}` and
  `X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_FEDERATION`. No token exchange.
- Provider token acquisition per the doc: AWS — a JWT from STS GetWebIdentityToken with audience
  `snowflakecomputing.com`; Azure — managed identity access token for resource
  `api://fd3f753b-eed3-462c-b6a7-a4b5bb650aad`; GCP — metadata-server ID token with audience
  `snowflakecomputing.com`; OIDC/Kubernetes — the provider-issued token (e.g. a projected
  service-account token file).
- Note: the SQL API reference header table omits WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_FEDERATION (doc
  inconsistency); if the header is omitted "Snowflake determines the token type by examining the
  token" — send it explicitly, verify live.

## Scope

1. `AuthProvider` implementation that acquires the provider token (fixed well-known endpoints per
   provider — no user-supplied token URL; OIDC via a file path handle), builds the header, and
   re-acquires before expiry (parse `exp` when the token is a JWT) inside the per-request bearer
   derivation; on 401 re-acquire exactly once (mirrors the JWT lane).
2. Profile handles: `<PREFIX>_AUTH=workload_identity`, `<PREFIX>_WIF_PROVIDER`,
   `<PREFIX>_WIF_TOKEN_FILE` (OIDC). README Configuration documents them.
3. Remove the quarantine from C7a for the new path; keep the experimental RFC 7523 code behind its
   feature or delete it with operator agreement.
4. Secret hygiene: provider tokens are credentials — covered by the leak gate (B6) and redaction.

## Tests

Header goldens per provider (mock provider endpoints); refresh-before-exp; 401 -> one re-acquire;
negative: the transport never sees a token-exchange request (assert). Live: add a WIF step to the
battery when an environment with a provider identity exists (optional; record skip typed).
acceptance_criteria: Closes only when the named tests/probes in the description pass, including the stated negative case; cite evidence in the close comment.
notes: Reality-check key: C7. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.

title: operator: provision a fresh Snowflake trial and credential handles for the live proof lanes (critical path)
description:
## Why this is the critical path

The project's core promise is a live connector. The only live evidence ever is a driver-level
run on 2026-06-25/26 against a 30-day trial that has since expired. Every live claim (CLI reads,
writes, JWT, cancel, catalog scan persistence, export) has been blocked on credentials since
2026-09-04 (beads bvf and w0i.13). No amount of offline work substitutes. Operator action.

## What to provision (never commit any of it; use the secret-provider convention)

1. A fresh Snowflake trial (https://signup.snowflake.com; trials need an email, no payment —
   plan "Free Trial Recommendation") or a dedicated low-cost test account.
2. A service user, and:
   - a programmatic access token (PAT) for it;
   - an RSA ≥2048 key pair with the public key registered (`ALTER USER ... SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY`)
     for the key-pair JWT lane;
   - optionally an OAuth access token for the OAuth lane.
3. Warehouse XS with auto-suspend 60 s.
4. A scratch database + schema where a WRITE role can CREATE/INSERT/MERGE/UPDATE/DELETE and
   COPY INTO a named internal stage (for the battery's write steps), and a separate READ-ONLY role
   (for L4's RBAC check).
5. Network policy allowing this host's egress IP.

## Handles to export (names only — values never in repo, beads, or logs)

`FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_TRIAL_{ACCOUNT,USER,AUTH,WAREHOUSE,DATABASE,SCHEMA,ROLE,PAT}`,
`FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_TRIAL_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM` (+ `_PASSPHRASE`), a second profile
`FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_TRIAL_RO_*` for the read-only role, plus `FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_LIVE=1`,
`FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_LIVE_PROFILE=trial`. Account identifiers must not be committed (A3).

## Acceptance

On this host: `fsnow profile validate trial --json` exits 0 (names only), and
`fsnow profile doctor trial --online --json` returns `data_source: "live"`. Record the date and
build sha (not the account) as a comment on bvf.

title: proof: capture redacted live wire transcripts during the credentialed battery as replay fixtures
description:
## Background (observed defect class)

The June 2026 live run found two protocol decode bugs that every document-derived fixture had
hidden (bead hij: `compressedSize` absent on inline partition 0; partition fetches return an
object `{"data": [...]}` rather than a bare array). All current fixtures are still
document-derived (crates/franken-snowflake-sqlapi/tests/fixtures/jsonv2_codec_cells.source.md says
so). Each credentialed run should permanently convert live behavior into no-account regression
fixtures.

## Design

1. A transcript recorder at the `RawHttp` seam under `SnowflakeHttpClient` (http crate), enabled
   only by `FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_CAPTURE_DIR` during live proof runs. It records request line,
   headers with Authorization -> `[REDACTED]` and host -> `<account>`, request body (SQL and
   bindings; secret literals redacted via B5), response status + headers + decompressed body with
   account, host, query ids and statement handles normalized to stable placeholders. Row data is
   kept only for the battery's synthetic tables/GENERATOR queries.
2. Output: `crates/franken-snowflake-testkit/fixtures/replay/<scenario>/<step>.json` with a
   provenance block `{captured_at, build_sha (H1), snowflake_version, doc_urls}`.
3. Before writing, run the canary + secret-shape scan over each transcript; refuse to write on any
   hit.
4. A replay test drives the PRODUCTION driver (`run_statement_with_auth` over a scripted RawHttp
   playing the transcript) and compares the resulting envelope with the captured live envelope
   (volatile fields zeroed).

## Acceptance

redactor as defense in depth; the pre-write canary/shape scan stays mandatory either way.

title: proof: cell-by-cell differential of typed results vs the official Snowflake Python connector, live in the same run
description:
## Background

Suite rule (/data/projects/AGENTS.md): "a claim is only as good as the arm it was measured
against" — the incumbent must run live, in the same invocation. For a connector, the first claim is
correctness: does fsnow return the same values as Snowflake's official driver for the same
statement? Typed decoding (C1) and Parquet (C2) are unverifiable without this. The codec's
timestamp-unit rules are document-derived and the docs are internally inconsistent (plan, Snowflake
facts).

## Design (a battery step, run only with credentials)

1. A type-matrix SELECT (every wire type; edge values; NULLs; TIMESTAMP_TZ with several offsets;
   NUMBER(38,0) near 10^37; scale 0..37; FLOAT NaN/Inf; BINARY; VARIANT/OBJECT/ARRAY; DATE before
   1970; TIME with 9-digit fractions) run through `fsnow query run --json` (typed.v1) and through
   `snowflake-connector-python` (pinned version, via `uv run --with ...`) against the same account
   and user in the same invocation.
2. Normalize both to canonical JSON (decimals as strings; timestamps RFC 3339 with offset; binary
   hex) and compare cell by cell; write a per-type verdict table.
3. Parquet: export the same result with `export run --format parquet` and compare pyarrow values to
   the connector's values.
4. Record connector version, fsnow build sha (H1), date; artifacts under the live run dir.
5. Optional later step (only then may a perf claim be made): fetch throughput for a 1M-row
   GENERATOR result vs the Python connector, with an A/A null (fsnow vs fsnow) that must come out
   ≈1.0.

## Acceptance

0 mismatches for the type matrix, or every mismatch filed as a bug bead with the evidence
(reporting a loss is a success).
acceptance_criteria: 0 mismatches for the type matrix, or every mismatch filed as a bug bead with the evidence (reporting a loss is a success).

title: proof: live probes for SQL-guard assumptions (nested comments, statement counting, account-level MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT)
description:
## Background

B3's lexer depends on two Snowflake behaviors that the docs do not settle: whether block comments
nest, and whether an account- or user-level MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT changes the SQL API default when
the request omits the parameter (JDBC docs say the parameter exists at account level and affects
"more than one driver"; SQL API docs are silent — both consulted 2026-09-23).

## Design (SELECT-only; nothing mutating is ever submitted)

1. Statement-count truth: submit a corpus of SELECT-only statements (dollar quotes, comments,
   semicolons in strings, nested comment shapes) with MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT pinned to "1". When
   the server's count differs it rejects the whole request ("Actual statement count N did not match
   the desired statement count 1") without executing anything. Compare with the lexer's count.
2. Nested comments: `SELECT 1 /* a /* b */ c */` and variants — record which parse.
3. Default override: on the throwaway service user, `ALTER USER <svc> SET MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT = 0`,
   submit `SELECT 1; SELECT 2` WITHOUT the parameter, record the result, then restore the setting.
   Needs the operator's agreement (it alters a user parameter on the test account).
4. Record findings with dates in docs/security_model.md and feed them back into B3's rules.

## Acceptance

Findings recorded; lexer agrees with the server on the whole corpus, or each disagreement is filed
as a bug.
acceptance_criteria: Findings recorded; lexer agrees with the server on the whole corpus, or each disagreement is filed as a bug.

title: proof: scheduled live canary with freshness surfaced in doctor and the claims ledger
description:
## Background (observed defect class)

Live evidence decayed silently for three months (June run -> September) while README claims grew,
and the trial account expired unnoticed. A one-off proof cannot keep a live claim true.

## Design

1. A scheduled job on this host (systemd timer or cron — never GitHub Actions) runs
   `scripts/live-proof-cli.sh` weekly with credentials from the secret provider.
2. It appends a redacted run record (date, build sha, per-step verdicts, durations) to a committed
   `docs/live_proof_state.json` (latest) and a run-log section in docs/live_proof.md.
3. `doctor --json` gains a `live_proof` check reading the committed state: last pass date and
   build sha, warning when older than 14 days or when the build sha differs from the running
   binary (H1). The claims ledger (A5) reads the same state.
4. On failure: non-zero exit plus a log line for the operator's notification channel; the failing
   step is filed as a bug bead by whoever triages.
5. Credential expiry (PAT defaults to 15 days — plan) surfaces as a typed failure, not silence.

## Acceptance

Two consecutive scheduled runs recorded; doctor shows freshness; a deliberately stale state
(date > 14 days) makes doctor warn (negative case).
acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive scheduled runs recorded; doctor shows freshness; a deliberately stale state (date > 14 days) makes doctor warn (negative case).

title: safety: profile doctor --online detects when a read profile's role can mutate data
description:
## Background

Client-side SQL classification can be bypassed (B3 found two bypasses). The enforceable read-only
guard is Snowflake's own RBAC: a read profile whose role cannot write cannot mutate, whatever the
classifier thinks. The plan wants read-only "enforced", and the Access Checklist asks the admin for
a "read-only role name".

## Scope

1. `profile doctor --online` runs `SELECT CURRENT_ROLE()` and `SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE <role>` (bound
   identifiers) and flags write-capable privileges (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, OWNERSHIP,
   CREATE *, ALL, APPLY *, EXECUTE TASK) as a warning: "this read profile's role can mutate data;
   create a read-only role". Note that inherited roles need `SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE` on each granted
   role — bound the recursion depth and report "partial" when capped. Cite the SHOW GRANTS doc URL
   and date.
2. Profile handle `<PREFIX>_READ_ONLY_EXPECTED=true` turns the warning into a hard failure (exit 3).
3. README Configuration recommends one read-only role per read profile.

## Tests

Parse fixtures of SHOW GRANTS output (document-derived) via the scripted execute seam: read-only
grants -> pass; INSERT grant -> warn; with READ_ONLY_EXPECTED -> fail (negative). Live: battery
step against the D0 read-only and write roles (both verdicts recorded).
acceptance_criteria: Closes only when the named tests/probes in the description pass, including the stated negative case; cite evidence in the close comment.
notes: Reality-check key: L4. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.

title: feat(lifecycle): no orphaned statements — SIGINT/SIGTERM/console-ctrl and drop fire the remote cancel (current runtime)
description:
## Background

README Architecture: "A submitted statement is modeled as an Asupersync bracket, so cancellation
always reaches Snowflake's remote cancel endpoint and no statement is orphaned." Plan: Ctrl+C maps
to CancelKind::User portably (signal-hook on Unix; a console-ctrl handler on Windows). An orphaned
statement keeps burning warehouse credits (plan: 60-second minimum per resume) and, for writes,
keeps mutating after the user thinks they stopped it.

This bead delivers the user-visible guarantee NOW on the current runtime (Asupersync 0.3.5);
bead E1b later replaces the hand-written guard with Asupersync 0.5's obligation/bracket primitive
after the migration (ufb), without changing behavior.

## Evidence (2026-09-23)

- Zero `bracket(` calls in code; the word appears only in doc comments
  (crates/franken-snowflake-sqlapi/src/driver.rs:9, sqlapi lib.rs:6). No Drop guard in production.
- No signal handling anywhere (no ctrlc, signal-hook, or SetConsoleCtrlHandler).
- Real today: cancel-on-error — every post-submit error or cancel branch calls cancel_locally /
  abandon_with_* under a cancellation mask; tested with FakeTransport
  (poll_transport_error_after_submit_fires_an_orphan_cancel,
  partition_fetch_error_fires_an_orphan_cancel,
  deadline_during_poll_routes_through_the_policy_cancel_with_deadline_kind; negatives
  happy_path...without_any_cancel, submit_panic_without_a_handle_does_not_attempt_cleanup).
- Therefore Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, process kill, a dropped future, or an MCP disconnect orphan the
  statement until the server STATEMENT_TIMEOUT (default 60 s, sent on every request — live.rs
  apply_session 1858-1873).
- TransportErrorCode::CancelledDuringConnect is declared (crates/franken-snowflake-http/src/lib.rs:2218)
  but never constructed; the plan wants a distinct receipt state.

## Scope (current runtime)

1. Signal handling: SIGINT/SIGTERM on Unix and SetConsoleCtrlHandler on Windows (a small,
   admissibility-checked crate such as `ctrlc` or `signal-hook`, or Asupersync's own signal
   support if it has one — check first) cancel the root Cx with CancelKind::User (SIGINT) or
   Shutdown (SIGTERM).
2. Drop-safe statement guard: once a statement handle exists, a guard object owns it; every exit
   path that has not reached a terminal state (success, server-side failure, confirmed cancel)
   issues the remote cancel POST under a short bounded budget before the process exits, including
   future drop and the signal path. A second Ctrl-C exits immediately after a bounded best-effort
   cancel.
3. The receipt records the terminal state `cancelled` (C6 mapping) with the CancelKind and the
   remote-cancel result; the documented exit code is returned.
4. Construct CancelledDuringConnect when the TLS handshake is interrupted and record it as a
   distinct receipt state.

## Tests (JSON-line logs)

Unit: drop the statement future mid-poll with a scripted transport -> the cancel request is
observed. E2E over F1's loopback mock: spawn the binary, the mock holds the statement in 202, send
SIGINT -> the mock observes POST /api/v2/statements/<handle>/cancel, receipt state cancelled,
documented exit code. Windows: same e2e through dsr (w0i.14). Teeth: removing the guard makes the
drop test fail (record in the close comment).
acceptance_criteria: Closes only when the named tests/probes in the description pass, including the stated negative case; cite evidence in the close comment.
notes: Reality-check key: E1. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.

comments.text:
PROGRESS 2026-09-24 (stays open). Scope item 1 (signals) done on Unix and compiled for Windows: SIGINT/SIGTERM while a live statement runs cancel its Cx (CancelKind::User / Shutdown) through signal-hook's flag API, so the driver's existing cancel-on-cancel path POSTs the SQL API cancel and the envelope reads outcome_kind=cancelled (FSNOW-5004); a second signal exits at once (130/143); with nothing in flight the default action is kept (Asupersync's dispatcher was not used: it swallows the signals process-wide, so a long `mcp serve` could not be stopped). Unit test a_pending_signal_cancels_the_statement_context (a pending interrupt flag cancels the statement Cx with User; terminate with Shutdown). Commit f122825, pushed; gates in the commit.
Windows: signal-hook routes Ctrl-C through the CRT's SIGINT; not yet run on Windows (needs dsr).
REMAINING: (2) drop-safe statement guard (future drop / panic / SIGKILL still leave the statement to the server STATEMENT_TIMEOUT); (3) receipt records the remote-cancel result; (4) CancelledDuringConnect receipt state; the F1 socket e2e with SIGINT -> observed cancel POST (written; runs with F1).

title: feat(mcp): MCP request cancellation and client disconnect cancel the running statement
description:
## Background

Plan + docs/agent_cli_contract.md: each MCP call is wrapped in an Asupersync `web::request_region`
so an agent disconnect drains the statement and partition fetchers as one owned region;
ctx.checkpoint() gives cooperative cancel points.

## Evidence

No `request_region` anywhere. MCP call (crates/franken-snowflake-mcp/src/lib.rs:881-886) is
checkpoint -> synchronous CLI call -> checkpoint; the CLI builds its own runtime whose Cx is not
linked to the McpContext, so an MCP cancel or a client disconnect cannot stop a running statement.

## Scope

Run tool handlers inside a request-scoped region linked to the MCP request context (use the
pinned Asupersync's request-region API — the plan named `web::request_region` when 0.3.x was
current; if it turns out to require 0.5, add a dependency on bead ufb instead of working around
it), and propagate `notifications/cancelled`, stdio EOF and HTTP connection close to
CancelKind::User so E1's lifecycle fires the remote cancel.

## Tests

stdio: start query_run against F1's mock held in 202, send notifications/cancelled -> mock sees the
cancel POST; HTTP: close the connection mid-call -> cancel POST. Negative: without the linkage the
mock sees no cancel within the test deadline.

title: feat(budget): real budgets on the live path — deadline, poll quota, child budgets, advisory cost quota with the 60 s floor
description:
## Background

Plan: "it cannot run away with cost" — per-query Budget (deadline + poll quota + cost quota)
propagated to partition fetchers via meet(); a cost breach surfaces as Cancelled(CostBudget) with
a distinct outcome; warehouse billing has a 60-second minimum per start/resume. README:
"a Budget with a cost quota".

## Evidence

The live root Cx has no budget (crates/franken-snowflake-cli/src/live.rs ~1748); poll, partition
and cancel requests use Budget::unlimited() (crates/franken-snowflake-http/src/lib.rs:2084, 2100,
2117, 2133; child_budget unlimited at 2480); query_budget / partition_child_budget are used only in
TUI tests; the only real meet() is the retry-attempt quota (lib.rs 914-936). A cost-budget cancel
cannot happen.

## Scope

1. Root budget: deadline from --statement-timeout (+ a small client margin) and poll quota from
   MAX_POLLS; child budgets via meet() for every partition fetch; cancel runs under a short masked
   budget.
2. Advisory cost quota: estimate credits = credits_per_hour(warehouse size from SHOW WAREHOUSES,
   cached per profile) x max(elapsed, 60 s when the warehouse was resumed) / 3600. Only when the
   profile sets `<PREFIX>_MAX_CREDITS` does a breach cancel with Cancelled(CostBudget) (C6
   outcome). Document that client-side credit accounting is advisory; STATEMENT_TIMEOUT stays the
   enforceable guard.
3. `budget_consumed` in the envelope reports real deadline/poll/cost usage.

## Tests (virtual time, scripted transport)

Deadline -> Cancelled(Deadline) -> outcome timeout + remote cancel; poll quota exhaustion; cost
breach with MAX_CREDITS -> cancelled/CostBudget; child budget tighter than parent. Negative: a
budget that is only recorded (not enforced) fails the deadline test.
acceptance_criteria: Closes only when the named tests/probes in the description pass, including the stated negative case; cite evidence in the close comment.

title: feat(caps): wire PlannerCx/TransportCx/WriteCx so read-only is compile-enforced, or retract the claim
description:
## Background

Plan "Asupersync Leverage Contract": the pure planning/validation/SQL-compile path runs under a
zero-capability Cx; the transport runs under a narrowed Cx; only the write-intent ladder widens
authority. README: "Reads run with read-only capabilities"; docs/security_model.md and
docs/write_intent_ladder.md claim enforcement; bead 9r9 claimed "(compile/test enforced)".

## Evidence

crates/franken-snowflake-core/src/capabilities.rs defines PlannerCx / TransportCx / WriteCx and
compile-time subset proofs with zero uses outside core. The http crate's TransportCaps is a marker
whose doc says "Public APIs accept &Cx directly for now" (crates/franken-snowflake-http/src/lib.rs:52-58).
Writes reuse the read transport unchanged (live.rs run_write_outcome).

## Scope (on Asupersync 0.5 — after ufb)

1. Planning / validation / SQL compilation functions take the zero-capability Cx.
2. Transport entry points take TransportCx; the write submit path requires a WriteCx that only
   the write ladder can mint after authorization.
3. Compile-fail tests (trybuild or `compile_fail` doctests) proving: the planner cannot call the
   transport; the read path cannot call the write submit.
4. If Asupersync 0.5's capability API makes this impractical, retract the claims in README and
   docs instead and close with that evidence (reporting a loss is a success).

## Acceptance

Compile-fail tests in the default test run, or documented retraction with evidence.

title: decision(operator): reconcile AGENTS.md with shipped behavior — frictionless writes, local Parquet, WIF sequencing, ci.yml deletion
description:
## Background

Four places where AGENTS.md (operator-owned policy) and shipped behavior disagree. Agents must
not silently pick a side; per RULE 0 the operator decides. Each item gives evidence and a
recommendation. Record the operator's answer as a comment on this bead; dependent beads read it.

## Decisions needed

1. **Write posture.** AGENTS.md:156-158 and docs/agent_cli_contract.md "Mutation Posture":
   "Any future DDL/DML/write path requires --dry-run, explicit --confirm, idempotency receipts,
   and append-only audit records." Commit 8c4a860 (2026-06-29, operator-authored) made writes
   execute directly once `<PREFIX>_WRITE_ENABLED=true`, with dry-run/confirm optional and
   `WRITE_REQUIRE_CONFIRM` re-arming the ceremony. Recommendation: keep the operator's
   frictionless default, update AGENTS.md + contract docs to match, and treat bead B4's
   integrity fixes (supplied tokens always checked, audit for every attempt, real idempotency,
   procedure opt-in) as non-negotiable.
2. **Local Parquet export.** AGENTS.md:69-70 and 107-108: local export is CSV/JSONL only;
   Arrow/Parquet deferred unless a forbidden-dependency-clean writer is proven. The
   `export|parquet` admissibility lane is clean (2026-09-23: 63 lanes, 0 violations; cargo tree
   shows no arrow/parquet/tokio crates). Recommendation: keep Parquet behind the `parquet`
   feature as experimental until bead C2 lands, then update AGENTS.md.
3. **Workload identity federation sequencing.** AGENTS.md:128: WIF "only after the first three
   lanes are stable". WIF landed 2026-09-19 while no lane has a live proof since June, and it
   implements a protocol Snowflake does not document for the SQL API. Recommendation: quarantine
   now (bead C7a), implement per docs after bvf proves PAT + JWT live (bead C7).
4. **.github/workflows/ci.yml.** On 2026-09-03 the operator said "clear the CI junk, we NEVER
   EVER use gh actions, ONLY /dsr". The deletion never landed: the file is tracked at HEAD,
   v0.0.3 and v0.0.4; repo Actions are now disabled (API: enabled=false). AGENTS.md:205 forbids
   the directory. Deleting a file needs fresh explicit written permission (RULE 1). Exact
   command to authorize: `git rm .github/workflows/ci.yml` then commit. Tracked on reopened bead
   egc.

## Acceptance

Operator answers recorded; AGENTS.md updated by or with permission of the operator; beads
C7, B4, C2 and egc updated with the decision.
acceptance_criteria: Operator answers recorded; AGENTS.md updated by or with permission of the operator; beads C7, B4, C2 and egc updated with the decision.

title: feat(stream): stream partitions into export sinks with bounded memory, --max-rows guard and NDJSON progress
description:
## Background

Plan "Performance Strategy": stream partitions into frames or local exports without holding full
result sets in memory; "Large result sets require --export, --max-rows, or an explicit
confirmation token". Contract: long-running commands emit typed NDJSON progress events on stderr
while the final envelope goes to stdout.

## Evidence

The full result is assembled in memory (crates/franken-snowflake-sqlapi/src/lifecycle.rs ~126);
`stream_partitions` / `PartitionSink` exist but are used only in tests; `export run` passes no row
cap, so the whole result sits in RAM before writing; no progress events exist (no bead covered
them).

## Scope

1. `export run` streams partition -> sink in order through the existing concurrent window; peak
   memory bounded by window x partition size.
2. `--max-rows` for export (default 1,000,000, configurable per profile) with an explicit override
   flag; exceeding it is a typed refusal before fetching further partitions.
3. NDJSON progress on stderr, opt-in with `--progress` (recommended default OFF: agents that
   capture stderr as diagnostics should not receive a new stream unasked; document the choice): `{"event":"partition_fetched","index":n,"rows":r,"bytes":b,"elapsed_ms":t}` plus
   submitted/polling/completed events. stdout remains the single envelope.
4. `query run` keeps its envelope row cap.

## Tests

Scripted 200-partition result: an instrumented counter proves buffered partitions never exceed
the window (negative: collect-all-then-write fails the bound); progress lines parse as JSON and
stdout is byte-identical with/without --progress; --max-rows refusal.
acceptance_criteria: Closes only when the named tests/probes in the description pass, including the stated negative case; cite evidence in the close comment.
notes: Reality-check key: E5. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.

title: proof: hermetic socket-level e2e — real binary to real Asupersync HTTP/TLS client to a loopback mock SQL API
description:
## Background

Plan "Testkit": an integration lane where the REAL CLI binary and MCP surface run full flows
against a mock SQL API server (202 -> 200 with gzip partitions, cancel, receipts, export).
AGENTS.md proof lanes: statement lifecycle through the mock server; cancellation tests that call
the cancel endpoint.

## Evidence

- No test drives binary -> Asupersync HTTP/TLS client -> driver -> mock over real sockets. CLI
  live tests replace everything below `execute_request` (crates/franken-snowflake-cli/src/live.rs
  ~2545 says this is "not transport-level proof"). scripts/e2e and the race suite drive only the
  statement state machine.
- The mock (crates/franken-snowflake-testkit/src/mock/server.rs, MockSqlApi) is an in-memory
  request -> response function, not a socket server (plan named fastapi_rust).
- The production host gate (validate_host, http lib.rs 628-721, commit 9297728) correctly refuses
  loopback; a hermetic socket test needs a compile-time test hook that can never reach release
  builds.

## Design

1. Cargo feature `testkit-endpoint` (never in release/dsr builds; capabilities
   feature_flags.testkit=true when on; RELEASE.md asserts false): allows
   `FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_TEST_ENDPOINT=https://127.0.0.1:<port>` plus a test CA PEM
   (`FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_TEST_CA`). The production validate_host path is unchanged.
2. Serve MockSqlApi over a real TLS listener (Asupersync server, or fastapi_rust as a
   dev-dependency per the plan — choose and justify; dev-only, admissibility-scanned).
3. Scenarios: 200 inline; 202 -> poll -> 200 multi-partition with gzip; 429 without Retry-After ->
   resubmit with the same requestId + retry=true; 408; 422; partition fetch error -> cancel POST;
   row-cap early stop; `query cancel` on a real handle; `query write` INSERT (receipt + audit);
   JWT 401 -> re-sign once; catalog scan -> dataset inspect -> query run --dataset.
4. Assertions: request bodies and headers (MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT "1" after B3,
   STATEMENT_TIMEOUT, QUERY_TAG, token-type header, requestId stability), envelopes, receipts,
   audit JSONL; canary PAT scanned across stdout, stderr, store and exports; one JSON-line log per
   step in an artifacts dir.
5. Runs in `cargo test -p franken-snowflake-cli --features live,mcp,testkit-endpoint`; added to
   RELEASE.md required proof and `dsr quality` on all three OSes (w0i.14).

## Negative case (proves no gate weakening)

The same test harness runs the plain `live` binary (feature off) with the test env set and asserts
FSNOW-2002 before any socket.

## Added in refinement round 1: operator-runnable wrapper

Add `scripts/e2e/socket_e2e.sh` that builds (or takes FSNOW_BIN), runs the socket e2e test binary,
and collects the per-step JSON-line logs, envelopes, request captures and store files into one
run directory with a summary.json (pass/fail per scenario, build identity from H1). Idempotent,
hermetic (strips credential env vars, sets FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_LIVE=0), exits non-zero on any
deviation — matching the plan's e2e-script requirement.

title: feat(catalog): real lineage edges and discovery breadth — view dependencies, PK/FK, tags, stages, file formats
description:
## Background

The plan calls the dataset-manifest model "the headline feature" and the graph crate must model
"foreign-key, view-dependency, and lineage edges discovered from the catalog"; catalog discovery
covers stages, file formats, and tags "where accessible". README calls `catalog graph` a lineage
graph.

## Evidence

Production graph building emits only Contains, DatasetObject and FieldColumn edges
(crates/franken-snowflake-graph/src/lib.rs 480-650); FK / view-dependency / lineage / stage /
file-format edges appear only in tests. Discovery reads only INFORMATION_SCHEMA DATABASES,
SCHEMATA, TABLES and COLUMNS (crates/franken-snowflake-catalog/src/discovery.rs 359-390); tags are
always empty (:541); `cycle_count` is always 0.

## Scope (all statements use positional bindings; record each doc URL + consult date)

1. View dependencies: INFORMATION_SCHEMA table function GET_OBJECT_REFERENCES(DATABASE_NAME=>...,
   SCHEMA_NAME=>..., OBJECT_NAME=>...) per view (bounded count, configurable), optionally
   SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES when the role can read it (note its latency).
2. Keys: SHOW PRIMARY KEYS / SHOW IMPORTED KEYS IN SCHEMA (column-level FK mapping), or
   INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_CONSTRAINTS + REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS where sufficient.
3. Tags: INFORMATION_SCHEMA TAG_REFERENCES / TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS table functions (may be
   edition-dependent — degrade gracefully).
4. Stages (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.STAGES) and file formats (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.FILE_FORMATS).
5. Insufficient privilege or unsupported edition -> `partial_success` with a typed warning naming
   the missing source; never a silent empty.
6. Snapshot schema version bump; catalog diff understands the new edges; graph edges typed
   (ViewDependsOn, ForeignKey, Tagged, StageFormat); cycle detection meaningful.

## Tests

Document-derived fixtures per query through the scripted execute seam; graph golden with FK +
view edges + a dependency cycle; privilege-error fixture -> warning (negative: failing hard or
returning silent empties fails). Live verification added as a battery step on bvf.

title: proof(identity): embed build identity in capabilities/receipts; live proofs record a self-reported exe sha256
description:
## Background

Suite rule (/data/projects/AGENTS.md, proof-class inflation): a result must carry provenance
including a binary SHA-256 self-reported from inside the process, so a harness cannot silently
measure the wrong build. [OBSERVED in this suite: a harness that could compare a build against
itself.]

## Evidence (2026-09-23)

- A HEAD dev build and the v0.0.4 release both report `version: "0.0.4"`; capabilities has no
  build field (keys: alternate_outputs, binary_aliases, commands, contract_version, crate_name,
  default_output, envelope_keys, environment, error_registry, exit_codes, feature_flags, non_goals,
  schema_version, tool_name, version).
- Commit 64a61dd makes scripts/live-proof-cli.sh and scripts/capture-jsonv2-golden.sh reuse any
  pre-built binary in $CARGO_TARGET_DIR with no commit or feature check; summary.json records no
  binary identity. A live proof could silently exercise a stale build.

## Scope

1. build.rs in the CLI crate captures git sha + dirty flag (`git rev-parse`, when available),
   else env `FSNOW_BUILD_SHA` (dsr sets it), else "unknown"; plus target, profile, enabled
   features, rustc version.
2. `capabilities`/`onboard` expose `build {version, git_sha, dirty, target, profile, features, rustc}`;
   `capabilities --with-exe-hash` computes sha256 of `current_exe()`.
3. Receipts and audit events record the build sha.
4. Live-proof scripts record git_sha + exe sha256 in summary.json and refuse a binary whose
   git_sha differs from HEAD unless `FSNOW_ALLOW_STALE_BIN=1` (then summary marks `stale: true`).

## Tests

capabilities contains the build fields; a dirty tree reports dirty=true; the script's selftest
refuses a mismatched binary (negative case).
acceptance_criteria: Closes only when the named tests/probes in the description pass, including the stated negative case; cite evidence in the close comment.
notes: Reality-check key: H1. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.
close_reason:
CLOSED (self-verified; not independently verified). Evidence, commits 3fd94f5/2a3f871 (+ earlier cca5f00):
1. build.rs: git sha + dirty (FSNOW_BUILD_SHA/DIRTY override, then git), target, profile, rustc, and a git-independent source_digest (SHA-256 over sha256sum lines of crates/**/*.rs, crates/**/Cargo.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock).
2. capabilities/onboard expose `build`; `capabilities --with-exe-hash` self-reports the executable's SHA-256 (verified equal to the on-disk file).
3. Receipts record build.git_sha + build.source_digest; audit events record build_git_sha.
4. scripts/live-proof-cli.sh and capture-jsonv2-golden.sh compare the binary's source digest with the working tree's (same recipe, proved equal to build.rs by the e2e test capabilities_reports_build_identity_and_self_hash) and refuse otherwise unless FSNOW_ALLOW_STALE_BIN=1 (summary.json: stale=true, both digests, git sha, exe sha256).
Observed defect fixed: an rch-built binary reported the previous commit (e8e7c55 while HEAD was fcc4bed) because the worker's .git is stale; with the digest, the selftest now passes without an override for a build of this tree (binary and tree digest 2e1b1e31...), and the planted mismatch is still refused. dirty=true is reported for a dirty tree.

comments.text: PROGRESS 2026-09-24 (stays open; defect found in verification): implemented build.rs identity (git sha, dirty, target, profile, rustc), capabilities.build + --with-exe-hash (self-reported SHA-256 equals the file on disk: 1e978011... in verify_batch.sh), receipts/audit record the git sha, live-proof-cli.sh and capture-jsonv2-golden.sh refuse a binary built from another commit unless FSNOW_ALLOW_STALE_BIN=1 (selftest: planted mismatch refused; override records stale=true). Test: cli_e2e capabilities_reports_build_identity_and_self_hash. DEFECT: an rch-built binary embeds the worker's stale .git state (reported e8e7c55 while HEAD was fcc4bed), so the identity check refuses every rch build (fails safe, but unusable). NEXT: embed a source digest (sha256 over the sorted crate sources + manifests + Cargo.lock) that the scripts recompute locally, and compare that instead of or in addition to git_sha.

title: release(gates): require fresh live battery, security suite, build identity, signed artifacts and a per-release run record
description:
## Background

docs/RELEASE.md is the release-readiness contract (dsr only, never GitHub Actions). The v0.0.4
release shipped with an exploitable MCP HTTP surface, corrupting Parquet export and README claims
that had outlived their evidence; the checklist had no gate that would have caught any of them.

## Evidence

- No v0.0.4 execution record in RELEASE.md, although dsr run dd041529 exists (manifest: source
  edd80c7 = the v0.0.4 tag, 6/6 targets native).
- Artifacts unsigned (`signed:false`, no .sigstore bundles); install.sh verifies sigstore only if
  cosign and a bundle both exist, so no signature is ever checked.
- aarch64-pc-windows-msvc has never been executed anywhere.
- No live-proof requirement in the checklist.

## Scope

Update docs/RELEASE.md required proof: claims ledger (A5) passes; live battery (bvf/D6) passed
within 14 days on the release build sha (H1); F1 socket e2e green; security suite (B1-B5 tests)
green; dsr full cross-OS tests (w0i.14); record every release run (dsr run id, manifest sha, hosts,
executed checks) — backfill v0.0.4; enable dsr artifact signing (minisign or sigstore) and make the
installer verify signatures when present, and say so honestly when absent; keep
aarch64-pc-windows-msvc labelled linked-not-executed until a host exists.

## Acceptance

RELEASE.md updated; the first release after this bead lands follows it and its run record cites every gate. The v0.0.5 security patch (B7) deliberately does NOT wait for this bead (it must not be blocked on live credentials); it ships under the existing checklist plus the new security tests.

## Added in refinement round 3: prove the fresh-clone source build

README: "--from-source builds from a fresh standalone clone: the FrankenSuite dependencies resolve
from crates.io, so no local sibling checkout is required." This was verified only by reading the
manifests and Cargo.lock (2026-09-23: no [patch], no out-of-workspace path deps, all registry
sources). Add to the release checklist a clean-environment smoke via `dsr canary` (container with
no /dp checkout): `install.sh --from-source --live --dest <tmp>` then `capabilities` reports the
expected version, build sha and live=true; record the run.
acceptance_criteria: RELEASE.md updated; next release (B7) follows it and its run record cites every gate.

title: proof: claims ledger mapping each README capability claim to fresh evidence, enforced in the release gate
description:
## Background (observed defect class)

The 2026-09-23 audit found ≥15 README/CHANGELOG/RELEASE.md sentences that were false or had
outlived their evidence — the live read+write claim outlived its only evidence (a June
driver-level run) by three months, "ci.yml was deleted" was never true, and CHANGELOG entries
claimed tests that silently skip. Checks are justified only against an observed defect class
(AGENTS.md "conformance metastasis" rule); this is one. Keep it lean.

## Design

- `docs/claims.toml`: one entry per load-bearing README capability claim:
  `id`, `anchor` (README heading + a verbatim substring that must exist), `evidence` = one of
  `test:<crate>::<test name>` | `live:<step>` (resolved against the committed live proof state,
  see D6) | `dsr:<run id>` | `manual:<note + date>`, and `max_age_days` for live evidence
  (default 30).
- README sentences carrying a load-bearing claim get an HTML comment `<!-- claim:<id> -->`.
- `scripts/check-claims.py`: (a) every tagged sentence has an entry and vice versa; (b) the
  anchor substring exists; (c) every `test:` names a test that exists
  (`cargo test -p <crate> -- --list`); (d) every `live:` evidence is within `max_age_days` of
  today AND for the release build sha when run in release mode; (e) prints one JSON line per
  claim `{id, evidence, verdict, reason}` and exits non-zero on any failure.
- Wire into docs/RELEASE.md "Required Local Proof" and `dsr quality`.

## Acceptance

- Passes on HEAD after A1 lands.
- Negative cases (teeth), each recorded in the close comment: a claim whose live evidence is 31
  days old fails; renaming a test that is cited as evidence fails; a tagged README sentence with
  no ledger entry fails.

## Added in refinement round 2: behavior before any live state exists

Until bvf/D6 produce `docs/live_proof_state.json`, every claim whose evidence is `live:` fails.
That is intended: while A1 has downgraded the live claims, the README carries no `live:` claims
and the check passes; the day a live claim is re-added, it needs fresh evidence.
acceptance_criteria: - Passes on HEAD after A1 lands. - Negative cases (teeth), each recorded in the close comment: a claim whose live evidence is 31 days old fails; renaming a test that is cited as evidence fails; a tagged README sentence with no ledger entry fails.
notes: Reality-check key: A5. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.

## Scope

   `nix` gating prerequisite is fixed upstream — see docs/dependency_admissibility.md), with a

description:

title: feat(lifecycle): adopt Asupersync 0.5 obligation/bracket for statement handles (structural, oracle-checkable)
description:
## Background

The plan's Asupersync leverage contract: "A submitted statement handle is modeled as an obligation
under bracket, so the remote cancel endpoint always fires on drop/cancel and no Snowflake statement
is orphaned." Bead E1 delivers the behavior on Asupersync 0.3.5 with a hand-written guard. After the
0.5 migration (ufb), adopt the runtime primitive so the guarantee is structural and checkable by the
lab runtime's obligation oracle (which the reopened DPOR bead o2o needs).

## Scope

1. Replace E1's hand-written guard with Asupersync 0.5's obligation (or bracket) primitive: the
   statement handle is an obligation that must be resolved (completed / cancelled /
   abandoned-with-reason); release = remote cancel under a masked short budget.
2. The lab runtime's obligation-leak oracle observes these obligations, so o2o's DPOR suite can
   assert "no leaked statement" from the runtime rather than a self-set ledger.
3. Behavior identical to E1 (its e2e tests stay green unchanged); README Architecture wording
   ("bracket") becomes true — update it and docs/asupersync_leverage.md.

## Tests

E1's full test set passes unchanged; a new lab-runtime test drops a statement future under the
oracle and asserts the obligation is resolved via cancel; teeth: an intentionally leaked obligation
is reported by the oracle.

title: feat(trace): default QUERY_TAG on every live statement and receipt-keyed RESULT_SCAN refetch
description:
## Background

Plan "Query Planning" and "Result Handling": set QUERY_TAG to the envelope command_id/trace_id on
every query for end-to-end traceability into Snowflake's own query history; re-fetch a
still-cached prior result cheaply with RESULT_SCAN('<query_id>') using the query_id stored in the
receipt store (Snowflake retains results about 24 h).

## Evidence

QUERY_TAG is set only with `--query-tag` or in dataset mode (raw `query run` sets none by default);
RESULT_SCAN is only an `export plan --query-id` source (crates/franken-snowflake-export/src/lib.rs
~231), not a re-fetch keyed on receipts. No bead covered either.

## Scope

1. Default QUERY_TAG `fsnow:<command_id>:<request_id>` on every live statement (reads and writes),
   overridable with `--query-tag`, disable-able per profile (`<PREFIX>_QUERY_TAG=off`); receipts
   record it.
2. `receipt refetch <receipt-hash> [--limit n] --json`: looks up the receipt's query_id and runs
   `SELECT * FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(?))` with a positional binding (verify RESULT_SCAN accepts a
   bind; otherwise validate the id strictly as a UUID-shaped query id); typed refusal when the
   receipt is older than 24 h ("result cache likely expired") or when Snowflake reports it gone.
   MCP tool `receipt_refetch`.

## Tests

Scripted execute seam: the submit body carries the default QUERY_TAG; `--query-tag` overrides;
refetch builds the RESULT_SCAN statement with the receipt's query_id; an unknown receipt ->
FSNOW-7002; a malformed query id is refused before submit (negative). Live verification as a
battery step on bvf.

title: security(mcp): authenticate and origin-restrict mcp serve --http (v0.0.4 is exploitable cross-origin)
description:
## Background

The plan's first differentiator is that an agent tool "cannot leak secrets". `fsnow mcp serve
--http <addr>` (README example: `127.0.0.1:3000`) is currently a credential-bearing endpoint that
any web page can drive.

## Evidence (reproduced 2026-09-23 against the shipped v0.0.4 x86_64 binary, loopback only)

- `OPTIONS /mcp` with `Origin: https://evil.example` + `Access-Control-Request-Method: POST` ->
  `200`, `access-control-allow-origin: https://evil.example`, `access-control-max-age: 86400`.
- `POST /mcp` initialize from that Origin -> 200 with the same ACAO header.
- `POST /mcp` tools/call `query_plan` from that Origin (after the initialize above; initialization
  is server-global, no session) -> executes and returns the envelope, readable by the page.
- crates/franken-snowflake-mcp/src/lib.rs:895-923 builds the server with no auth provider;
  fastmcp-transport 0.3.2's default CORS echoes the request origin. Host header is not checked
  (DNS-rebinding also works).
- Every tool is annotated `idempotent(true)` (lib.rs:875) and the server instructions say
  "Read-only Snowflake SQL API tools" (lib.rs:898) while `export_run` writes a local file
  (see B2) and `query_cancel` has remote side effects. Server logs
  "notifications/initialized ... Method not found".

Threat: a user runs `mcp serve --http` in a shell with live credential handles exported; any page
they visit calls `query_run` (reads warehouse data with their credentials and exfiltrates it) or
`export_run` (writes files).

## Scope

1. Bearer token required on `--http`: read from `FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_MCP_TOKEN` handle or generate a
   random 256-bit token at startup and print it once to stderr; constant-time comparison; never
   logged afterwards.
2. Origin policy: requests carrying an `Origin` header are rejected (403) unless the origin is in
   an explicit `--allow-origin <origin>` list (exact match, no wildcards); never echo arbitrary
   origins; preflight answered 403 by default.
3. Host header must be the bound address, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` (with port);
   otherwise 421/403 (DNS-rebinding defense).
4. Bind: loopback only by default; non-loopback bind requires `--allow-remote` and a token.
5. Tool exposure over HTTP: read-only tools by default; `export_run` and `query_cancel` require
   `--allow-tool <name>`. Truthful annotations per tool (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint,
   idempotentHint, openWorldHint); correct the server instructions text.
6. Handle `notifications/initialized`.
7. Upstream: note (comment) that fastmcp_rust's permissive default CORS should be fixed upstream;
   do not edit /dp/fastmcp_rust from this repo.
8. If the MCP library's HTTP transport cannot enforce 1-3, add a thin request filter in this
   crate in front of it (still no Tokio/hyper; Asupersync only).

## Tests (real loopback sockets, structured JSON-line log per request: method, path, tool,
origin, host, decision -> <artifacts>/mcp_http/events.jsonl)

(a) no token -> 401; (b) wrong token -> 401; (c) `Origin: https://evil.example` -> 403 for
preflight and POST; (d) `Host: evil.example` -> 421/403; (e) correct token, no Origin ->
tools/list OK; (f) export_run absent from tools/list over HTTP without `--allow-tool`;
(g) stdio behavior unchanged (tests/mcp_stdio.rs). Negative cases a naive fix fails: adding auth
but still echoing the Origin fails (c); blocking Origin but not Host fails (d).

## Acceptance

Tests green; README MCP section documents token/flags; capabilities lists the new flags; B7
ships it.
acceptance_criteria: Tests green; README MCP section documents token/flags; capabilities lists the new flags; B7 ships it.
notes: Reality-check key: B1. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.
close_reason:
CLOSED (self-verified; not independently verified). Evidence, 2026-09-24:
- crates/franken-snowflake-mcp/src/http_front.rs replaces fastmcp's permissive loop for `mcp serve --http`. Unit tests (mcp crate, 18 passed): missing/wrong token 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer; foreign Origin 403 even with a valid token and never echoed; preflight 204 + CORS only for --allow-origin; foreign Host 403; hidden tools refused and filtered; constant-time compare; Debug never prints the token.
- Socket tests (crates/franken-snowflake-cli/tests/mcp_http.rs, live,mcp lane, 3 passed): the v0.0.4 cross-origin exploit replayed -> 403 and not echoed; 401 without/with a wrong token; Host attacker.example -> 403; legitimate client initialize/tools.list/tools.call; export_run/query_cancel hidden unless --allow-tool; server refuses to start without FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_MCP_TOKEN (exit 64); per-request JSON decision lines on stderr include the refused 403/401 attempts and never the token.
- (g) stdio unchanged: tests/mcp_stdio.rs 1 passed.
- README MCP section and capabilities mcp.serve input_schema document --allow-origin/--allow-tool/--allow-remote and the token.
Shipping in a release is tracked by the release bead (B7), which needs the operator's go.

title: security(export): confine export run / MCP export_run output paths; never overwrite or follow symlinks implicitly
description:
## Background

`export run` (CLI) and the MCP tool `export_run` write a local file from query results.
crates/franken-snowflake-cli/src/live.rs:1338 does `std::fs::write(&out_path, &artifact.bytes)`:
no confinement, silently overwrites existing files, follows symlinks. The MCP `out` argument is
caller-controlled (mcp lib.rs ~382 schema, ~734 dispatch). Scenario: `export_run` with
`SELECT 'ssh-rsa AAAA... attacker'` and `out=~/.ssh/authorized_keys` (sshd ignores the CSV header
line) -> key injection; reachable from any web page while B1 is unfixed.

## Scope

1. CLI (human-invoked): create with `create_new` (O_EXCL) by default; `--overwrite` replaces only
   regular files — refuse when the target or any parent component is a symlink
   (`symlink_metadata`), write to a temp file in the same directory and atomically rename.
2. MCP: `out` must resolve inside a sandbox root: `FRANKEN_SNOWFLAKE_EXPORT_DIR`, default
   `<data_dir>/exports`. Reject absolute paths outside it, `..` traversal, symlinked components
   (canonicalize the parent and verify the prefix), Windows drive-relative and UNC paths. Over
   HTTP `export_run` is disabled unless `--allow-tool export_run` (B1).
3. Envelope reports the final canonical path, byte length and BLAKE3/sha256 of the artifact.
4. MCP annotation for export_run: destructiveHint=true, readOnlyHint=false, idempotentHint=false.

## Tests (JSON-line logs per case)

Unit tests for the path resolver: traversal, symlinked parent, absolute outside root, UNC,
drive-relative, existing file. E2E (scripted transport seam or F1 mock): MCP export_run with
`out="../../x"` -> typed refusal; existing file without --overwrite -> refusal; symlink target
with --overwrite -> refusal; happy path writes inside the root. Negative case a naive fix fails:
a string-prefix check without canonicalization fails the symlinked-parent test.

## Acceptance

Tests green; README export + MCP docs updated.
acceptance_criteria: Tests green; README export + MCP docs updated.
notes: Reality-check key: B2. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.
close_reason:
CLOSED (self-verified; not independently verified). Evidence, 2026-09-24:
- crates/franken-snowflake-cli/src/export_path.rs: create_new (O_EXCL) for new files; --overwrite = same-directory temp file + atomic rename, regular non-symlink files only; symlink/non-file targets refused. Sandbox mode (MCP export_run always passes --sandbox-out): relative only, no `..`, no root/drive prefix, no symlinked component (walked component by component after canonicalizing the root), resolved under <data dir>/exports.
- Unit tests (live lane): new vs existing file, symlink target refused even with --overwrite, traversal/absolute/empty refused, symlinked directory component refused (the case a string-prefix check without canonicalization fails), UNC/drive forms never resolve outside the root.
- End to end: scripted export run refuses a second write to the same path without --overwrite (no statement runs); MCP HTTP tools/call export_run with out="../../escape.csv" is refused ("may not contain `..`") before any statement.
- README export and MCP sections document the rules; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security.

title: security(sql): one shared Snowflake lexer for splitting, classification and redaction; close the $$ bypass; pin MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT=1
description:
## Background

Read-path safety (`query plan`/`query run`) and write classification (`query write`) rely on
hand-rolled scanners that do not understand Snowflake's lexical rules. The plan: "cannot run
away" and "no mutation without the explicit write-intent ladder".

## Evidence (reproduced on the HEAD `live,mcp` binary 2026-09-23, offline)

- `query plan --sql "SELECT $$ it's $$; <DROP> TABLE t"` -> ok, statement_kind=read (would be
  submitted on `query run`).
- `query write --sql "INSERT INTO t VALUES ($$it's$$); <DROP> TABLE x" --dry-run` with
  WRITE_ENABLED -> kind=insert, safety=dml: passes without WRITE_ALLOW_DDL.
- has_multiple_statements (crates/franken-snowflake-cli/src/lib.rs:4570), is_select_like
  (lib.rs:4667) and core guardrails.rs:446-576 do not handle `$$` dollar-quoted strings; the
  nested-block-comment assumption (lib.rs ~4735) is asserted without a documentation URL.
- Read path allows side-effecting functions: `SELECT SYSTEM$CANCEL_ALL_QUERIES(1)`,
  `SYSTEM$ABORT_SESSION`, `SYSTEM$CANCEL_QUERY`, sequence `NEXTVAL`.
- The only backstop is Snowflake's MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT default of 1 ("This is the default value
  used if you do not specify the MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT field" —
  https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/reference, consulted 2026-09-23). The live
  path never sets it: deterministic_session_parameters (live.rs:2430-2456) lacks it; the only
  reference is a #[cfg(test)] roundtrip in crates/franken-snowflake-sqlapi/src/request.rs:190.
  JDBC docs show `alter account set MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT = 0` exists and "affects more than one
  Snowflake driver/connector"
  (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/jdbc/jdbc-using, consulted 2026-09-23); whether
  it changes the SQL API default is undocumented (probe in D5).

## Scope

1. One Snowflake lexer module (in franken-snowflake-core, no new crate) producing tokens with
   spans: single-quoted strings with `''` and backslash escapes; `$$...$$` dollar-quoted strings;
   double-quoted identifiers with `""`; `--` and `//` line comments; `/* */` block comments
   (nesting per D5 evidence; until then ambiguous input is refused — fail closed); statement
   terminators; keywords case-insensitive.
2. Re-implement on it and delete the duplicated scanners: statement counting, read
   classification, write classification (core write_intent classify), SQL preview normalization,
   and the secret-literal redactor (B5).
3. Always send `parameters.MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT = "1"` on every live submit (read and write),
   except the explicit multi-statement opt-in (L1).
4. Read path: typed refusal (FSNOW-3001 family) for side-effecting SYSTEM$ functions and NEXTVAL;
   documented allowlist of benign SYSTEM$ functions (e.g. SYSTEM$TYPEOF,
   SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION).

## Tests (JSON-line log per corpus case: input hash, expected, actual, verdict)

- Corpus `crates/franken-snowflake-core/tests/fixtures/sql_guard_corpus.jsonl`
  (input, expected statement count, expected class) with every case from the 2026-09-23 audit
  (dollar quotes, nested comments, `-- ;` newline, trailing semicolon, full-width semicolon,
  NUL, backslash-escaped quotes, CALL, EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, BEGIN, SHOW;DROP, COPY INTO @stage,
  PUT/GET/REMOVE/USE/ALTER SESSION, EXPLAIN DELETE, unterminated comment) plus new ones.
- Metamorphic properties (deterministic generator, fixed seeds): inserting comments or
  whitespace between tokens, changing keyword case, or changing string-literal contents never
  changes the statement count or the class; re-joining token texts reproduces the input.
- Submit-body assertion that MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT is "1" (scripted execute seam now; F1 later).
- Teeth: run the corpus once against the OLD functions and record ≥2 failures in the close
  comment (proves the corpus catches the known bypass).

## Acceptance

Corpus 100% pass; both `$$` bypasses refused; MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT pinned; docs/security_model.md
documents the lexer rules with doc URLs and dates.

## Added in refinement round 2: `$` is not always a dollar quote

Snowflake uses `$` in several non-string positions; the lexer must not open a dollar-quoted string
there, or the fix creates new false refusals (or new bypasses): identifiers containing `$`
(`SYSTEM$TYPEOF`, `a$b`, `"x$y"`), positional column references in stage queries (`SELECT $1, $2
FROM @stage`), session variables (`$var`, `SET var = ...` is refused anyway), and `$$` inside a
single-quoted string or comment. Only a `$$` token in code context opens a dollar-quoted string,
closed by the next `$$`. Add each form to the corpus with the expected count/class; cite the
Snowflake "String & binary data types" / dollar-quoted constants doc page (URL + date).
acceptance_criteria: Corpus 100% pass; both `$$` bypasses refused; MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT pinned; docs/security_model.md documents the lexer rules with doc URLs and dates.
notes: Reality-check key: B3. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.
close_reason: Landed in fcc4bed. SELF-VERIFIED (no independent verifier; re-executed against the acceptance text): (1) corpus: core sql_lexer unit + metamorphic tests and CLI regressions pass (core 77, cli default 75+10, cli live,mcp 86+10+1); (2) both $$ bypasses refused on the rebuilt HEAD live,mcp binary (FSNOW-3002), while the pre-fix binary accepted them on 2026-09-23 (teeth); (3) MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT="1" asserted on the submitted request in the scripted live test; (4) docs/security_model.md 'SQL Statement Guard' documents rules + doc URLs. Deviations: corpus lives inline in unit tests and the selftest fixture rather than a separate JSONL file; side-effect detection is an allowlist of read-only SYSTEM$ functions. Not covered here: server-truth probes (D5, needs credentials).

title: security(write): make the write ladder rungs real — check supplied tokens, key/expire them, real idempotency, audit every attempt, gate procedures
description:
## Background

The write-intent ladder (plan "Write And Update Support", docs/write_intent_ladder.md) promises a
typed safety classification, an allowlist, an idempotency id, an exact confirmation token, an
execution receipt and an append-only audit. The operator made writes frictionless by default
(commit 8c4a860, see A4) — that is fine — but several rungs are cosmetic.

## Evidence (HEAD, 2026-09-23)

a. With WRITE_ENABLED and no WRITE_REQUIRE_CONFIRM, `query write ... --confirm confirm:insert:0000`
   (a token that matches nothing) proceeds toward execution (reached the transport host check,
   FSNOW-2002). `require_exact_confirmation` is armed only by WRITE_REQUIRE_CONFIRM
   (crates/franken-snowflake-cli/src/lib.rs:3574). README: the token "executes only the same
   statement on the same profile".
b. Token = `confirm:<kind>:<FNV(profile, SQL)>`: unkeyed, computable offline, never expires,
   reusable.
c. Idempotency: every submit uses a fresh `unique_request_id` (live.rs:2534, used ~1811), so
   replaying a confirmed write re-executes it; the ladder's stable id is only recorded.
d. `require_append_only_audit: false` (lib.rs:3576); failed or indeterminate writes after submit
   write no audit record (run_write_outcome, live.rs:369-424).
e. The allowlist rung is generated from the classified kind, so it always passes
   (lib.rs:3568-3581).
f. `call my_proc()` -> kind=call, safety=procedure, needs only WRITE_ENABLED; a procedure can run
   DDL/GRANT, bypassing WRITE_ALLOW_DDL.
g. `put file:///etc/hosts @s` -> accepted (kind=put); the SQL API does not support PUT/GET
   (https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/sql-api/intro "Limitations of the SQL API",
   consulted 2026-09-23). `use role accountadmin` -> accepted (kind=use); USE / ALTER SESSION /
   BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK / SET are supported only inside multi-statement requests (same page).
h. `copy into 's3://bucket/x' from t credentials=(...)` -> kind=copy_into_table, safety=dml
   (core write_intent.rs ~647 recognizes only `@` stages); it is an unload to an external
   location with inline credentials.

## Scope

1. A supplied `--confirm` must match (profile, SQL, kind) in every mode -> FSNOW-3008 on mismatch.
2. Tokens: HMAC-SHA256 keyed by a per-data-dir random secret (file mode 0600 in the data dir;
   Windows ACL equivalent), embedding issued-at; expire after 15 minutes (profile-configurable
   `WRITE_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS`); single-use (consumption recorded in the audit log; reuse refused).
3. Idempotency: derive the SQL API requestId from the ladder idempotency id for confirmed writes;
   resubmission (including a replay of the same --confirm) sends the same requestId with
   `retry=true` so Snowflake returns the prior result instead of re-executing (cite the SQL API
   reference section on requestId/retry with URL + date in code and docs).
4. Audit every write attempt: refused, dry_run, submitted, succeeded, failed, indeterminate;
   `require_append_only_audit: true`.
5. CALL / EXECUTE IMMEDIATE / EXECUTE TASK require a new opt-in `WRITE_ALLOW_PROCEDURES=true`
   (documented: procedures can run DDL/GRANT).
6. Refuse PUT, GET, USE, ALTER SESSION, BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, SET with typed FSNOW-3010
   ("not supported by the Snowflake SQL API as a single statement") citing the doc URL.
7. Classify COPY INTO external locations (quoted `s3://`, `gcs://`, `azure://` URLs) as
   `unload_external` (named/user/table stages `@...` stay in the existing DML class), flag inline
   CREDENTIALS, and require `WRITE_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=true`.
8. Optional profile allowlist `WRITE_ALLOWED_KINDS=insert,merge,...`; when unset the rung is
   documented as kind-derived (no pretend check).

## Tests (JSON-line logs; scripted execute seam, later F1)

Mismatched token refused in default mode; expired token refused; reused token refused; replay of a
confirmed write sends the SAME requestId with retry=true (assert request body); failed write
produces an audit line; CALL refused without opt-in; PUT -> FSNOW-3010; external COPY classified
`unload_external`. Negative case a naive fix fails: a token check that only runs under
WRITE_REQUIRE_CONFIRM fails the first test.

## Acceptance

Tests green; docs/write_intent_ladder.md, README Writes, capabilities/handbook updated; decision
from A4 reflected.

title: security(redaction): secret-bearing SQL literals leak into envelopes and the append-only audit log
description:
## Background

The plan's first differentiator: the connector "cannot leak secrets" (no secret in config, Debug,
JSON output, panic text). SQL statements themselves can carry secrets (passwords, cloud
credentials, encryption keys), and the local store is append-only by design, so any leak into it
is permanent.

## Evidence (HEAD `live,mcp` binary, 2026-09-23, offline dry-run)

`query write --profile demo --sql "alter user x set password = '<canary>'" --dry-run --json`
(WRITE_ENABLED + WRITE_ALLOW_DDL): the canary appears verbatim in `data.redacted_sql_preview`
(sic), `data.confirm_command`, `safe_next_commands[0]`, and is persisted to
`<data_dir>/query_audit_log.jsonl`. Redaction only matches known token prefixes
(live.rs:1898-1904, lib.rs:3686-3691). Receipts store the normalized SQL, so live runs persist
the same literals.

## Scope

1. On the B3 lexer, redact string literals that are values of secret-bearing parameters:
   PASSWORD, CREDENTIALS=(AWS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_KEY, AWS_TOKEN, AZURE_SAS_TOKEN, ...),
   ENCRYPTION=(MASTER_KEY, ...), OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN, SECRET_STRING
   (CREATE SECRET), API_KEY, TOKEN, plus the existing shape detectors (JWT `eyJ`, `AKIA`, ...).
   Cite the Snowflake doc page for each parameter family (URL + date) in docs/security_model.md.
2. One redaction function applied at every sink: envelope fields (previews, confirm_command,
   safe_next_commands, error text), receipts, audit log, stderr, MCP responses, TUI log pane,
   exports' provenance records. The SQL submitted to Snowflake is not redacted (it must run);
   stored hashes use the keyed hash from B4 (not reversible).
3. Rename `redacted_sql_preview` only if it stays accurate (it must be redacted).

## Tests

Canary corpus: one statement per secret-bearing clause with a unique canary; run each through
dry-run, write refusal paths, and the scripted live execute seam; scan stdout, stderr, receipts,
audit JSONL, export provenance and MCP responses for every canary -> zero hits (JSON-line log per
sink). Teeth: the pre-fix redactor leaks ≥1 canary (record in the close comment).

## Acceptance

Zero canary hits across all sinks; docs updated.
acceptance_criteria: Zero canary hits across all sinks; docs updated.
notes: Reality-check key: B5. Cross-references to other keys (A1, B3, C1, ...) resolve via the key map in the epic fsnow-agent-ergonomic-cli-rc-2026-09-23-oj0.

The remaining item (tokens/idempotency ids as an unkeyed FNV hash of the SQL printed in envelopes, which allowed offline guessing of a short secret) is gone with B4's rungs (commit 3fd94f5): tokens are random per dry run (two dry runs of the same statement give different tokens, verified on the binary), and the statement is bound in the store only through an HMAC-SHA256 digest under a per-data-dir key (0600). Earlier evidence stands: shared redactor covers secret-bearing SQL literals at every sink, canary corpus e2e zero hits across stdout/stderr/store (secret_sql_literals_never_leave_the_process), teeth: v0.0.4 leaks the canary 4x + 1 store file, HEAD 0/0 (b5_teeth.sh on both binaries).

Docs cite the Snowflake reference pages (docs/security_model.md). Tests: core families/edge/shell-embedded (negative case a lexer-based redactor fails); cli_e2e secret_sql_literals_never_leave_the_process (5 statements x refusal, dry-run and confirm paths; stdout, stderr and every file in the data dir: zero hits). title: catalog: operator arity-1 JSON Schema rejects single-element-array value that the runtime validator accepts
description:
Found via fresh-eyes review (read-only; verified firsthand against source).

LOCATION: crates/franken-snowflake-catalog/src/operator.rs describe_operator_json_schema Exact{count:1} arm (~L147) vs predicate.rs value_count (L191).

BUG: for arity-1 operators (eq, neq, lt, lte, gt, gte, contains) the published JSON Schema sets value = scalar_value_schema() (oneOf string/number/integer/boolean) with required:[value] — arrays forbidden. But value_count() returns values.len() for Some(Value::Array), so a single-element array [5] yields count 1 and OperatorArity::Exact{1}.accepts(1) passes. So the server-side validate_leaf accepts {op:eq,value:[5]} while the agent-facing schema (surfaced via MCP dataset_describe_operator and the --jsonschema CLI path) rejects it. The two contract sources disagree; a strict client validating against the schema refuses a payload the server honors, and vice versa. (The planner then first_value()s and binds only element 0.)

VERIFY: validate_predicate(LeafPredicate{op:"eq", value:Some(json!([5]))}) -> Ok; the same JSON against describe_operator_json_schema(eq) -> fails (array vs scalar).

FIX: align them. Either accept a 1-item array in the Exact{count:1} schema (oneOf[scalar, {type:array,minItems:1,maxItems:1,items:scalar}]), or tighten value_count so arrays are not counted as 1 for Exact{count:1} operators (reject arrays where a scalar is required). operator.rs/predicate.rs are under active edit; left for the catalog owner.

title: [review] graph Mermaid label escaping is ineffective (backslash not entity; brackets unescaped) -> injection/corruption
description:
crates/franken-snowflake-graph/src/lib.rs:831-837 (escape_mermaid_label), used in the flowchart node labels (~lines 335-347)

escape_mermaid_label does value.replace('\\',"\\\\").replace('"',"\\\"").replace('|'," ").replace('\n'," ") — i.e. it C-style backslash-escapes the quote. Mermaid does NOT interpret backslash escapes inside ["..."] node text; the documented way to include a quote is the HTML entity #quot; / ". So a label containing a double-quote terminates the ["..."] early and can inject additional Mermaid syntax. It also leaves '[', ']', '{', '}', '(', ')' unescaped, any of which corrupt the node/flowchart, and only strips '\n' (not '\r' or U+2028/U+2029).

Trigger: a quoted Snowflake identifier like  EV"]click["x  (legal as a quoted identifier, and pulled verbatim from catalog discovery) flows into format!("...{}", dataset.object) producing a label that breaks the node bracket and injects a second node/edge. This is output corruption / Mermaid injection from catalog-derived names, not style.

Fix: escape per Mermaid rules — encode '"' as " (or #quot;), and escape or strip the structural chars [ ] { } ( ) and all line separators (\n \r U+2028 U+2029). Note: SVG output (escape_xml) is correct; only the Mermaid path is affected. Relates to fsnow-native-snowflake-connector-w0i.9.
close_reason: Fixed in 0d9d492: escape_mermaid_label now HTML-entity-encodes all Mermaid-reserved chars (quote, brackets, braces, parens, pipe) plus &<> and collapses all line separators, replacing the ineffective C-style backslash escaping. Regression tests added (unit + injection-via-object-name integration test). SVG escape_xml path was already correct.
